title: Father kills his son
article: Dead is nine-year-old Justin Stochmal and his father, Michael Stochmal, who both died at the family's home at 6 Plentywood Bay in North Regina.
Police say three other children who lived at the house escaped injury but their mother received injuries that were non life- threatening.
Police say they essentially know what happened but they were continuing their investigation over the weekend in order to find out why the incident happened.
"That's really the big question, is why," said Sgt. Richard Bourassa of the Regina Police Service.
"This is really a horrible tragedy involving a lot of people," Bourassa said.
Counsellors have been brought in to assist surviving members of the family to deal with their grief and shock, Bourassa said.
Police say they were alerted that there was a problem in the house when they received a 9-1-1 call from inside the house at 9:55 p.m.
Police responded immediately but a second call from a neighbouring house was received at 9:57 p.m. indicating that a child had been stabbed and was lying on the ground.
When the police arrived, they discovered the father (Michael Stochmal) who was shouting and in the process of taking his clothes off on the street.
Bourassa said the elder Stochmal appeared to be delusional, drunk, and was also, possibly, on drugs.
A total of eight police officers were required to subdue Stochmal.
But, when Stochmal was placed into a police car, he went into an apparent cardiac arrest.
Efforts by the police to revive him were unsuccessful.
Attempts by EMS workers to revive both the man and the boy were also unsuccessful and both were subsequently pronounced dead.
Police say they are continuing their investigation but that the incident appears to have begun as a family dispute.
At some point before the incident began, a man believed to be Michael Stochmal apparently drove a truck up on to the lawn of the house, got out of the truck and entered the house.
While an exact timetable of events is not available, Bourassa said the whole incident unfolded "very quickly" and was over in a matter of minutes.
The split-level house where the incident happened is on a quiet bay in a comfortable middle class area of the city where crimes of violence are relatively rare.
"This whole situation is unusual," Bourassa commented Sunday.
"It is not something we normally see."
